headline: Record revenue and backlog beat Rocket Lab's own guidance
summary_short: Rocket Lab's Q2 2026 revenue rose 62.0% y/y (16.8% q/q) to a record $234.1M, beating its own $225M-$240M revenue and 33%-35% GAAP margin guidance, while net loss widened slightly q/q to $49.3M (-$0.08/share) even as Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $8.8M, well inside its $20M-$26M guided range.
summary_long: Q2 2026 revenue grew 62.0% y/y (16.8% q/q) to a record $234.1M, driven by demand across launch and space systems. GAAP gross margin was 36.1%, beating the 33%-35% guided range, and non-GAAP gross margin rose to 41.5% from 36.9% y/y. Operating loss narrowed y/y to $57.5M but widened slightly q/q; GAAP net loss was $49.3M (-$0.08 diluted EPS), while Adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to $8.8M from $27.6M y/y, well inside the prior $20M-$26M guide. Cash rose to $2,129.5M and equity to $3,492.2M after large ATM equity issuance; convertible notes fell to $13.1M. Backlog reached a record $2.36B (+137% y/y). Rocket Lab guided Q3 2026 revenue to $250M-$265M and an Adjusted EBITDA loss of $17M-$23M.

drivers.explanation: Company attributes the y/y jump to demand growth 'across all areas of our business,' citing more than $1 billion in new Q3 launch and space-systems contracts signed since quarter-end.
Not explained beyond overall program execution; the 36.1% margin beat the company's own 33%-35% guided range for the quarter.

Not explicitly explained; the release's own reconciliation shows the y/y improvement occurred despite a higher intangible-amortization add-back from the Mynaric/Motiv acquisitions ($7.2M vs $1.8M a year ago).
Narrowed y/y as revenue and gross-profit growth outpaced higher operating expenses; the non-GAAP table shows $8.6M of M&A-related transaction costs this quarter versus $5.0M a year ago.
Beat the company's own $20M-$26M guided loss range; management framed results as continuing 'massive momentum' behind record revenue and backlog.
Widened q/q as operating expenses (R&D + SG&A, +$9.6M q/q) grew slightly faster than gross profit (+$8.1M q/q), a gap not offset by higher net interest income.
Follows the wider net loss q/q, compounded by a higher weighted-average diluted share count (629.7M vs 605.4M q/q) from continued ATM equity issuance.
Rose mainly on $1.53 billion of gross proceeds from ATM equity offerings, per the six-month cash-flow statement, which does not break the figure out by quarter.
CEO cites a record $2.36 billion backlog, up 137% y/y, plus more than $1 billion of new contracts signed in Q3 to date across launch and space systems.
Not explained in the release; the balance sheet shows the balance falling from $36.9M (Q1 2026) to $13.1M, continuing its decline from $152.4M at 2025 year-end.

Growth reflects additional paid-in capital rising to $4.61B from $2.74B at year-end 2025, consistent with large ATM equity raises and stock issued for acquisitions, partly offset by a wider accumulated deficit.

CEO Peter Beck called it 'another fantastic quarter,' citing record revenue and backlog, the closed Mynaric and Motiv acquisitions, and the announced Iridium deal as steps toward a vertically-integrated 'tier-1 space power.'
